target.title: fix(mcp): standalone apps stop hanging on stalled gateway requests
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users opening a standalone MCP App could see it remain stuck indefinitely when its Gateway view request stalled before completing the response body. The same unbounded request path could also leave standalone tool and resource operations waiting forever.

## Why This Change Was Made

The standalone host now applies the shared 30-second Gateway request deadline across both the initial fetch and response-body consumption. It retains each request controller through the page lifecycle, aborts pending work when the page closes, and preserves the existing ticket, sandbox, and operation boundaries.

## User Impact

Standalone MCP Apps now fail with a clear `MCP App request timed out` message instead of hanging indefinitely when the Gateway response stalls. Closing the page also cancels pending standalone requests.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/mcp-app-standalone.test.ts` — 13/13 passed.
- `./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1 src/gateway/mcp-app-standalone.ts src/gateway/mcp-app-standalone.test.ts` — passed.
- Targeted Oxlint for both changed files — passed.
- Core and core-test `tsgo` checks — passed.
- Real Chromium proof loaded the production standalone shell against an HTTP 200 response whose JSON body stalled; after 30 seconds the request was aborted and the page displayed `MCP App request timed out` — 1/1 passed.
- `git diff --check` — passed.
